summary_html: Agency or court authorizes **immediate medical or psychological care** when delay endangers life or safety. Federal statutes support medical access and confidentiality exceptions for child protection.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — permits emergency medical actions for abused/neglected children  
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — multidisciplinary response and medical-exam standards

primary_citations.citation_text: California - Penal Code §§ 11164–11174.3 (CANRA – Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act)
California - Welfare & Institutions Code § 300 et seq. (Juvenile dependency proceedings)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 22 - Social Security (DSS Child Welfare Regulations)
Title 11 - Law (DOJ Child Abuse Central Index)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents and children have a constitutional right to live together free of governmental interference, that children may not be removed without a court order absent reasonable cause to believe of imminent danger of serious bodily injury, and that intrusive medical examinations of children in protective custody may not be conducted without a court order or parental notice and consent.
key_cases.relevance: Is the governing Ninth Circuit authority on examining or treating a child in protective custody without a court order or parental notice and consent.
key_cases.quote: Parents and children have a well-elaborated constitutional right to live together without governmental interference.

key_cases.case_name: San Joaquin County Human Services Agency v. Marcus W.
key_cases.holding: The court reversed an order compelling a dependent minor to undergo periodic blood transfusions over his religious objection, holding the juvenile court lacked jurisdiction to issue the order because the procedural requirements of Welfare and Institutions Code section 369 were not satisfied.
key_cases.relevance: Is the California authority on the statutory procedure a court must follow before authorizing medical treatment for a dependent child over the objection of the child or parent.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the juvenile court lacked jurisdiction to issue the order because the requirements of Welfare and Institutions Code section 369 were not met.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that the case plan and case records provisions of the federal Child Welfare Act, 42 U.S.C. sections 671(a)(16) and 675(1), create rights enforceable by foster children under section 1983, while the guardian ad litem provision does not, and reinstated the children's substantive due process claims arising from harm suffered in state custody.
key_cases.relevance: Arose in part from the agency's failure to approve necessary medical treatment for a child in its custody.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the case plan provisions of the CWA, codified at §§ 671(a)(16) and 675(1), are enforceable through § 1983.
